philosophy.title: Ebru Art

what.title: What is Ebru?
what.body: Ebru is the traditional Turkish art of floating natural pigments on thickened water and transferring the pattern onto paper. Every piece is unique; the same composition cannot be remade.

how.title: How is it made?
how.body: Pigments are dropped onto the prepared water with a brush or stylus. The design is guided with a comb, stylus or breath, then lifted onto paper. The artist guides — water has the final word.

unique.title: Why is each piece unique?
unique.body: Flow, pigment and timing intersect differently every time. Each Ebru carries the spirit of that moment as a singular, unrepeatable touch.

battal.title: Battal Ebru
battal.body: The foundational form. Pigments are left to spread freely, creating organic rings and natural blooms.

gelgit.title: Gelgit Ebru
gelgit.body: Formed with back-and-forth strokes of a stylus or brush. Wavy, rhythmic lines define its character.

tarakli.title: Taraklı Ebru
tarakli.body: Drawn with special combs to create ordered, combed textures — geometry meeting fluid motion.

cicekli.title: Çiçekli Ebru
cicekli.body: Stylized floral motifs worked over a gelgit or battal ground. Requires refined stylus control.

hatip.title: Hatip Ebru
hatip.body: Symmetrical, medallion-like forms opening from the center. Dense color rings and balanced composition are typical.

kumlu.title: Kumlu Ebru
kumlu.body: A grainy, sand-like texture created through pigment consistency and tray conditions — a fine particulate surface effect.

about.title: About the Artist
about.intro: I am an artist who bridges worlds—the ancient and the contemporary, the fluid and the structured, the organic and the geometric.
about.para1: Through the centuries-old Turkish art of Ebru marbling, I explore the unpredictable beauty of water and pigment. Each piece is a meditation on impermanence and the acceptance of what emerges from chaos.
about.para2: My photography practice complements this fluidity with deliberate composition—finding poetry in architecture, light, and negative space. Where Ebru embraces spontaneity, photography demands intention. Together, they form a dialogue about control and surrender.
about.para3: Based between tradition and innovation, I create work that invites contemplation and celebrates the duality of the creative process.
about.quote: Art is not about perfection—it's about presence. It's about showing up to the blank page, the still water, the empty frame, and trusting what wants to emerge.
